A three-digit code $\overline{abc}$ ($a \in \{1,\dots,9\}$, $b,c \in \{0,\dots,9\}$) is **Adaptive** if for each of the three digit positions, shifting that digit by exactly one unit (up or down, with wraparound mod 10) produces a multiple of 11.

**Divisibility by 11.** A three-digit number $\overline{abc}$ is divisible by 11 iff its alternating digit sum $S = a - b + c$ satisfies $S \equiv 0 \pmod{11}$. Since $S \in [-8, 18]$, this means $S \in \{0, 11\}$.

**Wraparound shifts.** Shifting a digit $d$ by $\pm 1$ (mod 10) produces an actual integer change $\Delta$:
- $d \in \{1,\dots,8\}$: $\Delta \in \{+1, -1\}$
- $d = 0$: $\Delta \in \{+1, +9\}$ (up: $0\to1$; down: $0\to9$)
- $d = 9$: $\Delta \in \{-9, -1\}$ (up: $9\to0$; down: $9\to8$)

The new alternating sum after shifting position 1 is $S + \Delta_a$; position 2 is $S - \Delta_b$; position 3 is $S + \Delta_c$. Each must be able to reach $\{0, 11\}$.

## Eliminating 100–110

For $N \in \{100,\dots,109\}$: $a=1, b=0$, $S = 1+c \in \{1,\dots,10\}$. For $N=110$: $S=0$.

The required $\Delta$ for positions 1 & 3 is $\{-S,\, 11-S\}$; for position 2 it is $\{S,\, S-11\}$. Checking each $S$:

| $S$ | $\{-S,11-S\}$ | In any allowed set? | $\{S,S-11\}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | $\{0,11\}$ | No (no allowed set contains 0 or 11) | — |
| 1 | $\{-1,10\}$ | $-1$ ✓ (digits 1–9) | $\{1,-10\}$: $1$ ✓ (digits 0–8) |
| 2 | $\{-2,9\}$ | $9$ only via digit 0 | — |
| 3–8 | $\{-S, 11{-}S\}$ | neither value in any allowed set | — |
| 9 | $\{-9,2\}$ | $-9$ only via digit 9 | — |
| 10 | $\{-10,1\}$ | $1$ ✓ (digits 0–8) | — |

Now check each candidate 100–110:

- **100** ($S=1$): position 3 has $c=0$, allowed $\Delta\in\{+1,+9\}$, but needs $\{-1,10\}$ — neither matches. ✗
- **101–108** ($S=2,\dots,9$): position 1 requires $\Delta_a \in \{-S, 11-S\}$, but $a=1$ only offers $\{+1,-1\}$. For $S=2$: need $\{-2,9\}$ ✗; $S=3..8$: need values not in $\{+1,-1\}$ ✗; $S=9$: need $\{-9,2\}$, but $a=1\ne9$ ✗.
- **109** ($S=10$): position 1 needs $\{-10,1\}$, $a=1$ offers $+1$ ✓; but position 3 has $c=9$, allowed $\Delta\in\{-9,-1\}$, needs $\{-10,1\}$ — neither matches. ✗
- **110** ($S=0$): impossible (no allowed $\Delta$ is 0 or 11). ✗

So **no number in 100–110 is Adaptive**.

## 111 is Adaptive

Take $N = 111$: $a=b=c=1$, $S = 1-1+1 = 1$.

- **Position 1** ($a=1$, allowed $\Delta\in\{+1,-1\}$, need $\{-1,10\}$): choose $\Delta=-1$, i.e. $1\to0$. Result: $011 = 11 = 11\times1$. ✓

All three positions admit a valid shift producing a multiple of 11. Since every number from 100 to 110 fails, **111 is the smallest three-digit Adaptive code**.
